earlierFailuresAndRepairs.observation: A solution-wide no-restore build lacked assets files for three previously unbuilt research tools.
earlierFailuresAndRepairs.repair: Restored existing declared dependencies during normal solution build. No project or package reference changed.

earlierFailuresAndRepairs.observation: Child test processes initially selected system .NET 6/7; the server and computer-use MCP process exited with code 150.
earlierFailuresAndRepairs.repair: Selected the installed user .NET 10 SDK for child processes and reran checks. The launcher also checks SDK resolution and forwards its path.

earlierFailuresAndRepairs.observation: Offline identity sync showed raw fetch errors; an old reminder test expected a model call after identity refresh had already failed.
earlierFailuresAndRepairs.repair: Localized the early offline error, retained the unsent draft and verified due-check failure, release and successful recovery.

earlierFailuresAndRepairs.observation: Routing a media command through the common entry point could let reminder words in a song title reach channel reminder preparation.
earlierFailuresAndRepairs.repair: Web and QQ skip reminder preparation for media commands; browser and signed-channel regressions cover the case.

earlierFailuresAndRepairs.observation: A concurrent full-browser run had one intermittent sync failure while scenarios shared mutable gateway configuration and a latest-request log.
earlierFailuresAndRepairs.repair: Serialized the shared fixture and collected browser diagnostics. The complete 35-scenario run passed with 29 passed and 6 environment-gated skips. This is test isolation, not a product concurrency benchmark.

limits: QQ outbound and model providers are controlled test substitutes; this is not live QQ login or a real-model acceptance run.
Licensed MMD model cases and opt-in external research, renderer and Minecraft cases remain skipped as listed.
No DSH plugin installation, autonomous social posting, voice training, held-out study or thesis scientific gate was executed.
The in-memory queue remains process-local. External tool actions are not automatically replayed and have no cross-crash exactly-once guarantee.
